title: Nuances
intro: Parler des règles et donner des conseils, imaginer ce qui va arriver avec if, déjouer les faux amis et choisir entre -ing et to : ton anglais devient précis.

boss.name: Les Jumeaux Faux-Amis
boss.taunt: On ressemble à des mots français, mais méfie-toi… Actually, tu vas perdre. Et ça, ce n'est pas une déception, c'est une certitude !
boss.defeat: Quoi ?! Tu as vu clair dans notre jeu… On retourne se cacher à la library — euh, à la bibliothèque !

units.title: Obligations et conseils
units.goal: Dire ce qui est obligatoire, interdit, conseillé ou possible avec must, have to, should et might.

lesson.text: [[must]], [[should]], [[might]], [[may]] et [[could]] sont des **modaux** : des petits verbes spéciaux. **Jamais de -s**, **jamais de to** après, et toujours le verbe de base : [[She must go.]] (et non *she musts to go*).

lesson.title: Obligation : must ou have to ?
lesson.text: [[must]] = obligation forte, souvent une règle écrite ou ce que **toi** tu juges nécessaire : [[You must wear a helmet.]] [[have to]] = obligation qui vient de l'extérieur (règlement, horaire). Lui, il se conjugue comme un verbe normal : [[She has to leave.]], [[Do you have to work?]] Au passé, [[must]] n'existe pas : on dit [[had to]] ([[I had to wait.]]).

head: Forme
Sens
Exemple
rows: don't have to / doesn't have to
conseil (tu devrais / tu ne devrais pas)

lesson.title: Possibilité : might, may, could
lesson.text: [[might]], [[may]] et [[could]] = « peut-être » : [[I might be late.]] = Je vais peut-être être en retard. Pour dire « peut-être pas », utilise [[might not]] ou [[may not]] : [[She might not come.]] Attention : [[couldn't]] ne veut **pas** dire « peut-être pas », mais « n'a pas pu / ne pourrait pas ».

LE grand piège : [[mustn't]] ≠ [[don't have to]] ! [[You mustn't come.]] = Tu n'as **pas le droit** de venir. [[You don't have to come.]] = Tu n'es **pas obligé** de venir (mais tu peux !). Truc : « interdit » = [[mustn't]] ; « pas obligé » = [[don't have to]].

Pour parler de santé : « J'ai mal à la tête » = [[I have a headache]], « J'ai de la fièvre » = [[I have a fever]]. Et [[advice]] (des conseils) est **indénombrable** : [[some advice]], [[a piece of advice]], jamais *an advice* ni *advices*.

grammar.q: The museum is free today. You ___ pay to go in.

grammar.q: I'm not sure yet, but I ___ go to the party. I'm very tired. (possibilité négative)

grammar.q: Hockey players ___ wear a helmet. It's the rule.

grammar.q: My sister ___ get up early on Sundays. She can stay in bed.

grammar.q: Last year, we ___ wear a uniform at school.

grammar.q: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early tonight.
grammar.explain: Pour un conseil : should + verbe de base.

grammar.q: ___ your dad have to work on Saturdays?
grammar.explain: Have to se conjugue comme un verbe normal : Does your dad have to…?

grammar.q: Students ___ use their phones during the test. It's forbidden!
grammar.explain: Interdit → mustn't (must not).

grammar.q: She musts wear glasses to read.
grammar.explain: Un modal ne prend jamais de -s : she must.

grammar.q: He have to take his medicine every morning.
grammar.explain: Have to se conjugue : he has to.

grammar.q: Did you must wait a long time?
grammar.explain: Must n'existe pas au passé : Did you have to wait…?

grammar.q: Can you give me an advice?
grammar.explain: Advice est indénombrable : some advice (ou a piece of advice), jamais an advice.

grammar.q: I have a fever, so I might stays home tomorrow.
grammar.explain: Après might : verbe de base, sans -s.

reading.title: The New Pool Rules
reading.text:
Every summer, Zoé works as a junior lifeguard at the community pool in Ottawa. This year, the pool has some new rules, and Zoé has to explain them to the kids.

First, swimmers must take a shower before they go into the water. Children under eight must stay with an adult at all times. Nobody is allowed to run near the pool, because the floor is wet and slippery. You can bring a snack, but you mustn't eat it inside: food is only allowed on the grass outside.

Some things are not obligatory. Swimmers don't have to wear a swimming cap, and they don't have to bring their own towel, because the pool lends towels for free.

On sunny days, Zoé gives the same advice to everyone: "You should wear sunscreen, and you should drink lots of water." Last week, a boy called Félix didn't listen. He stayed in the sun all afternoon without a hat. In the evening, he had a headache and a fever, and he had to stay in bed the next day.

Tomorrow, the weather might be stormy. When there is thunder, the pool has to close. Zoé hopes the storm won't come, because she might lose a day of work.

She sells sunscreen at the pool.

choices: She is probably paid only when the pool is open.
She has to swim in the storm.

units.title: Si…
units.goal: Parler de vérités générales et de conséquences probables avec if, unless, when et as soon as.

lesson.text: Pour parler d'une condition, l'anglais a plusieurs « conditionnels ». Ici, les deux premiers : le **zéro** (c'est toujours vrai) et le **premier** (c'est probable, dans le futur).

lesson.title: Le conditionnel zéro
lesson.text: [[If]] + présent, présent : pour les vérités générales et les faits scientifiques. [[If you heat ice, it melts.]] Ici, [[if]] veut presque dire [[when]] (chaque fois que).

lesson.title: Le premier conditionnel
lesson.text: [[If]] + présent, [[will]] + verbe : pour une situation future probable. [[If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home.]] **Jamais de will après if** : *If it will rain* ❌. Même règle après [[when]], [[as soon as]], [[unless]], [[before]] et [[after]] quand on parle du futur : [[I'll call you as soon as I get home.]]

head: Mot
Sens
Exemple
rows: [[If I see Maya, I'll tell her.]]
quand (c'est sûr que ça va arriver)
[[Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus.]]
[[As soon as it stops raining, we'll go out.]]

lesson.text: Piège de francophone : en français, on dit « Quand je **serai** grand… » avec un futur. En anglais, c'est le présent : [[When I'm older]], jamais *When I will be older*. Et [[unless]] contient déjà la négation : [[unless you study]] = si tu n'étudies pas. Ne dis jamais *unless you don't study*.

La virgule : quand la phrase commence par [[If]], on met une virgule au milieu : [[If it snows, we'll go skiing.]] Quand [[if]] est au milieu, pas de virgule : [[We'll go skiing if it snows.]] Les deux ordres sont corrects !

reading.title: The Green Challenge
reading.text:
This month, Noah's class is taking part in the Green Challenge. The rules are simple: if a class saves the most energy and produces the least garbage, it wins a trip to a nature park.

On the first day, Noah looked inside the recycling bin and was shocked. It was full of food! "If we put food in the recycling bin, the plastic can't be recycled," he explained. "Food goes in the green bin." So the class made posters for every bin.

Next, Amir checked the classroom. The lights were on all day, even at lunch, and the tap in the corner was always dripping. "If nobody uses the lights at lunch, we'll save a lot of energy," he said. "And if we fix that tap, we'll stop wasting water."

Some students complained. "Unless everyone helps, we won't win," Noah told them. As soon as they saw the results of the first week, they changed their minds: their class was in second place!

Now the whole class has new habits. When they finish their lunch, they sort everything carefully. Plastic bags are gone, and everyone brings reusable containers. The final results will come out next Friday. If they win, Noah will bring his camera to the park.

units.title: Les faux amis
units.goal: Éviter les faux amis qui piègent les francophones et choisir le bon mot.

lesson.text: Un **faux ami**, c'est un mot anglais qui ressemble à un mot français… mais qui veut dire **autre chose**. Les jumeaux Faux-Amis adorent te piéger !

lesson.title: Comment les reconnaître ?
lesson.text: Quand un mot anglais ressemble à du français, **méfie-toi** et regarde le contexte. [[Actually]] sert surtout à corriger ou à nuancer : [[I thought it was easy. Actually, it was hard.]] [[Eventually]] veut dire que quelque chose arrive **enfin, après beaucoup de temps** : [[He eventually found his keys.]] Pour « actuellement », dis [[currently]] : [[She's currently in Vancouver.]]

Le piège le plus fréquent : « J'attends l'autobus » = [[I'm waiting for the bus]], et non *I'm attending the bus*. Et « Je suis sensible » = [[I'm sensitive]]. Si tu dis [[I'm sensible]], tu dis « je suis raisonnable » !

reading.title: Félix in Toronto
reading.text:
Last summer, Félix spent two weeks with his cousin Olivia in Toronto. His English was good, but the false friends tricked him again and again.

On the first day, Olivia asked him, "What do you want to do today?" Félix answered, "I want to go to the library to buy a comic book." Olivia laughed. "Actually, you can't buy anything at the library. You mean the bookstore!"

The next day, Félix told Olivia's mom that he was very sensible, because sad movies always made him cry. She smiled kindly and explained that he meant "sensitive". A sensible person makes good, reasonable choices.

Later that week, they attended a lecture about dinosaurs at a museum. When it was over, Félix said, "That was a great reading!" Olivia whispered, "In English, a reading is something you read. This was a lecture!"

At the end of the trip, Félix felt a little disappointment, because he was making so many mistakes. But Olivia told him, "Don't worry. Everyone learns this way. Eventually, the false friends won't trick you anymore."

Now Félix has a notebook of false friends. He reads it every night, and he currently has more than fifty words in it.

questions.q: What does Félix do now to fight the false friends?
choices: He reads his notebook of false friends every night.
He goes to the library every day.

units.title: Gérondif ou infinitif
units.goal: Choisir entre verbe + -ing et verbe + to, et changer le sens avec stop, remember, forget et try.

lesson.text: Quand deux verbes se suivent, le deuxième prend soit **-ing**, soit **to + verbe**. Ça dépend du **premier** verbe. Il faut les apprendre par cœur, mais il y a des trucs !

head: Groupe
Verbes
Exemple
rows: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, keep, suggest, practise, can't stand
want, decide, hope, plan, promise, refuse, learn, manage, afford
interested in, good at, thanks for, before, after, without, instead of

lesson.title: Après une préposition : toujours -ing
lesson.text: Après [[in]], [[at]], [[for]], [[about]], [[before]], [[after]], [[without]], [[instead of]]… le verbe prend **-ing** : [[I'm good at drawing.]] [[He left without saying goodbye.]] En français on dit « avant d'aller », mais en anglais : [[before going]], jamais *before to go*.

lesson.title: Les verbes qui changent de sens
lesson.text: [[stop]] + -ing = arrêter une activité : [[I stopped eating candy.]] / [[stop]] + to = s'arrêter **pour** faire autre chose : [[I stopped to eat.]] — [[remember]] + to = ne pas oublier une tâche : [[Remember to call Grandma!]] / [[remember]] + -ing = se souvenir d'un moment passé : [[I remember meeting her.]] — [[forget]] + to = oublier de faire : [[I forgot to lock the door.]] / [[I'll never forget]] + -ing = ne jamais oublier un souvenir : [[I'll never forget seeing the ocean.]] — [[try]] + to = faire un effort : [[I tried to open the jar.]] / [[try]] + -ing = tester une solution : [[Try adding some salt.]]

Piège : en français, « j'aime nager » = verbe + infinitif. Mais [[enjoy]] veut **toujours -ing** : [[I enjoy swimming]], jamais *I enjoy to swim*. Même chose pour [[suggest]] : [[He suggested going to the park]], jamais *He suggested to go*. À l'inverse, [[afford]] et [[decide]] veulent **to** : [[I can't afford to buy it.]]

reading.title: Maya's Big Decision
reading.text:
Maya loves cycling. Every weekend, she rides her old bike along the Ottawa River. Last spring, her bike kept getting flat tires, so Maya decided to buy a new one. There was just one problem: she couldn't afford to pay for it.

At first, she asked her parents for help, but they refused to give her the money. Instead, her dad suggested finding a summer job. Maya didn't enjoy hearing that, but she promised to try.

She started walking her neighbour's dogs every morning. On weekends, she also offered to cut the grass for families on her street. Some days were hard. Maya can't stand getting up early, and one of the dogs kept running after squirrels! But she never stopped working.

Every evening, she remembered to put her money in a jar, and she avoided spending it on candy. By the end of August, she had enough.

When she rode her new bike for the first time, she felt very proud. "I'll never forget buying this bike with my own money," she said. Next summer, she hopes to save money for a helmet camera.

choices: Her parents told her to buy one.
